findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hard-coded as plaintext Lambda environment variables in the Terraform configuration. These values are committed to source control, stored in cleartext in Terraform state, and readable by any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, providing a direct path to credential theft and lateral movement.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment block containing secret material is encrypted only with the AWS-managed default key rather than a customer-managed CMK with a restrictive key policy. Any principal able to read the function configuration receives the decrypted secrets with no additional key-level authorization boundary.

The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is past AWS end-of-support and no longer receives security patches for the runtime or its bundled libraries, leaving the execution environment exposed to known unpatched vulnerabilities.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or NACL enforcement point. Given that the function holds credential material in its environment, this removes a network control that would otherwise constrain exfiltration after a compromise.
